notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 87-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.72, creatinine 1.05-1.09, hemoglobin 11.8-13.3, platelets 299-300, sodium 139-140, wbc 8.3-8.9; vitals dbp 72-76, heart_rate 80-83, map 88-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 119-126, spo2 96-97, temp 37-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.04-1.09, hemoglobin 10.6-11.7, platelets 291-302, sodium 140, wbc 8.4-9; vitals dbp 73-77, heart_rate 79-84, map 89-93, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 118-125, spo2 96-97, temp 36.9-37.2
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 87-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
